0.0.n: With の, this identifies whose company it is.

0.1.n: Links 私 to 会社 to show belonging.

0.3.n: Marks the company as the setting where this work schedule applies.

0.4.n: Added after で to make the company setting the topic.

0.5.n: 時 marks the hour, and 半 adds half an hour.

0.6.n: Marks 9時半 as the time identified as the start of work.

0.7.n: A noun referring to the beginning of the working day.

0.8.n: Politely ends the statement identifying the starting time.

1.0.n: Refers to the part of the day before noon.

1.1.n: Makes the morning the topic of this scheduling explanation.

1.2.n: Combines with で to describe working without other people.

1.3.n: With 一人, marks how the speaker wants to concentrate.

1.4.n: Used as a noun with をする; 集中する without を is also common.

1.5.n: Marks 集中 as what the speaker wants to do.

1.6.n: する changes to したい to express the speaker's desire.

1.7.n: Connects the desire to concentrate alone with the resulting scheduling choice.

1.9.n: 系 adds the sense of a category or type to 作業.

1.10.n: Links 作業系 to 仕事, describing the kind of work.

1.11.n: Refers to the jobs or tasks placed in the morning schedule.

1.12.n: Marks 仕事 as what gets put into the schedule.

1.13.n: 入れる + ています describes a regular scheduling practice here, with a polite ending.

2.0.n: Followed by の to identify the speaker's own work.

2.1.n: Links 私 to the following phrase メインの仕事.

2.2.n: An English loanword used with の to describe 仕事.

2.3.n: Links メイン to 仕事 so it describes the job as primary.

2.4.n: Refers to the speaker's professional role.

2.5.n: Marks 私のメインの仕事 as the topic of the explanation.

2.6.n: An English loanword naming the speaker's primary role.

2.7.n: だ takes the form な before ので after a noun.

2.8.n: Introduces the reason these activities form the speaker's main work.

2.10.n: An English loanword referring to the speaker's work group.

2.11.n: Links チーム to みんな, identifying which people are meant.

2.12.n: チームのみんな refers collectively to the team members.

2.13.n: Marks the team members as the recipients of the communication.

2.14.n: The name of the workplace messaging service used here.

2.15.n: Marks Slack as the tool used for communication.

2.16.n: 連絡する means to contact someone; this segment joins たり to form 連絡したり.

2.17.n: In 連絡したり, presents contacting people as one example rather than an exhaustive list.

2.19.n: Refers to details defining how a product or system should work.

2.20.n: Marks 仕様 as what the speaker thinks about.

2.21.n: The plain dictionary form appears before など to give another example activity.

2.22.n: Signals that the listed activities are examples, not the complete set.

2.23.n: Connects the examples ending in など to 作業.

2.24.n: Groups the preceding example activities together as work tasks.

2.25.n: Marks the described tasks as what makes up the main work.

2.26.n: Used as a noun here, identifying these tasks as the bulk of the work.

2.27.n: Adds a polite ending to the statement about the primary tasks.

0.lit: At my company, 9:30 is the start of work.
0.tip: では combines で, marking the setting, with は, making that setting the topic.

1.lit: Mornings, because I want to concentrate alone, I put task-oriented work into the schedule.
1.tip: 入れています means regularly putting work into the schedule here, rather than physically putting something inside.

2.lit: Because my main job is project management, tasks like contacting everyone on Slack and considering specifications are the main part.
2.tip: たり and など show that the activities mentioned are examples, not a complete list.
